pc1: An evaluative axis, not a personality factor — good traits against bad ones, cutting across Conscientiousness, Intellect and Agreeableness at once. Steering along it is the only direction that produces emergent misalignment.
pc2: Warmth. Mostly Agreeableness, blended with emotional flatness — Unemotional and Unexcitable sit alongside Cold and Harsh.
pc3: Extraversion, almost exactly. The cleanest factor recovery in the analysis; steering changes response length tenfold and alignment not at all.
pc4: Imaginative against unimaginative, but split between Intellect and Emotional Stability. Above the noise floor, not a single factor.
pc5: An anxiety axis — but at 3.1% of variance it sits where training noise could produce comparable structure. Not interpreted.
pc6: No cosine above 0.13 with any Goldberg factor. Not distinguishable from noise.
fa1: Agreeableness, recovered cleanly — ten Agreeableness markers at each pole, correctly signed.
fa2: Conscientiousness. One intruder on the negative pole, consistent with it being the least separable factor in this space.
fa3: Extraversion. Recovered by both methods, because it is the factor least entangled with the others.
fa4: Intellect — and the clearest demonstration that rotation works: PCA gave it no component of its own.
fa5: Emotional Stability, the weakest of the five on every measure. Treat with the most caution.
